pages.text: "Mom, I will stay behind here." Riri hid behind a fish box. Today she was helping at Mom's stall. "I just have to say welcome..." Her voice faded away.
Lolo waved both arms in front of the stall. "Welcome!" Riri covered her hot cheeks with both hands. "I want to do it too, but everyone might look at me."
A customer in a hat arrived. Riri breathed in. While she chose between now and later, the customer passed. She kept gripping the box corner.
Mom crouched beside Riri. "Riri, you do not have to start loudly." "Can I be quiet?" Riri fiddled with her hat brim.
"Of course. Say welcome, even softly!" Mom whispered into Riri's ear. Riri whispered into Mom's ear too. "Welcome..."
"Now come forward past just one box." Riri stepped past one. A customer came just then. She whispered, "Welcome." The customer nodded.
Riri counted boxes on her fingers as she moved forward. "One, two, three." Now she was at the very front. Though her legs trembled, she did not step back.
A customer with a big basket strode up. Riri took a deep breath and called, "Welcome!" Her voice reached the end of the market.
At the stall, Riri greeted every passing customer. "One, start very softly! Two, one box forward! Three, a little louder each time!" Lolo clapped beside her.
Mom sat on a crate, put Riri on her lap, and wrapped both arms around her. "Start small, and shy feelings pass." Held close, Riri looked toward the stall front and smiled. "Say welcome, even softly!"
